question: Can one learned image-guided module upsample spatial features from previously unseen vision encoders, channel dimensions, and input/output resolutions without encoder-specific retraining while preserving the original representation space?

key_findings.claim: AnyUp makes the learned key path invariant to the number and ordering of input feature channels by applying the same spatial filter bank independently to every channel, normalizing across filters, and averaging channel responses into a fixed-width representation.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 1 defines M learned k-by-k basis filters shared across all N input channels. Each channel's filter responses are softmax-normalized over the basis and then averaged over N, so the downstream attention network always receives M channels even when the source encoder dimensionality changes. The raw low-resolution feature vectors remain the attention values, preserving their native dimensionality in the output.

key_findings.claim: The model combines that canonical feature summary with high-resolution RGB queries, but restricts cross-attention to a local window so each output vector is a linear combination of nearby coarse feature vectors rather than the entire feature map.
key_findings.evidence: The architecture adapts JAFAR's high-resolution-to-low-resolution attention: image features form queries, downsampled image information plus the canonicalized feature map form keys, and unprocessed source features form values. Section 4.2 reports that global JAFAR attention sometimes selects distant unrelated regions; relative windows remove those paths and reduce the attention work from HWhw to HW times a fractional local area. Appendix B uses NATTEN with a relative window size of 0.2.

key_findings.claim: Crop supervision supplies higher-resolution target features without evaluating the backbone on a full very-high-resolution image, and two consistency losses constrain sensitivity to RGB augmentation and drift from the source feature space.
key_findings.evidence: Training downsamples a full image to the crop resolution, extracts its coarse feature map, and supervises only the corresponding region of the upsampled prediction against features computed on an original-resolution local crop. The objective adds cosine-plus-MSE target loss, self-consistency between clean and augmented guidance images, and input consistency between source features and a downsampled output. This avoids the full 448-by-448 reference pass used by the compared low-ratio training strategy.

anchors.section: C.1 Self-Consistency Regularization and Data Augmentations

key_findings.claim: On the paper's DINOv2-centered linear-probing suite, AnyUp is at or near the best reported result across semantic segmentation, surface normals, and absolute and relative depth, while also allowing arbitrary resolution ratios.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 2-4 compare bilinear, FeatUp, LoftUp, JAFAR, and AnyUp. The reported aggregate rows include COCO mIoU 62.16, surface-normal RMSE 31.17, ADE20k mIoU 42.43, absolute-depth RMSE 0.4755 with delta-1 0.8216, and relative-depth RMSE 0.3378 with delta-1 0.9233 for AnyUp. Across varied feature/output sizes, it leads most settings and trails the best competitor slightly only for the stated 16-to-112 case.

anchors.section: Table 4, Upsampling from Any to Any Resolution

key_findings.claim: Cross-encoder experiments support inference-time transfer, but the strongest universality evidence is heterogeneous rather than exhaustive: a DINOv2-trained instance transfers to SigLIP2 and DINOv3, and multi-backbone training improves held-out DeiT while slightly reducing in-domain DINOv2 quality.
key_findings.evidence: Table 6 tests a DINOv2 ViT-S-trained AnyUp on SigLIP2 and DINOv3 and compares it with encoder-specific LoftUp and JAFAR instances. Figure 6 varies DINOv2 model size. Table 7 trains on five encoders and holds out DeiT; the paper reports improved average and held-out performance, alongside a small DINOv2 regression attributed to reduced overfitting to encoder-specific positional artifacts.

key_findings.claim: The empirical gains do not establish recovery of spatial information absent from the coarse tokens; the architecture is explicitly limited to image-guided reweighting of existing low-resolution feature vectors.
key_findings.evidence: The authors identify the single-attention assumption as a limitation: each output is a linear combination of source features, even though individual patch channels may encode sub-patch information that a more expressive decoder could extract. The ablation without the feature-map contribution to key computation remains competitive, showing that RGB position/color matching is already a strong prior and making semantic reconstruction versus edge-aware interpolation an important unresolved distinction.

method.core_idea: Learn a fixed-width, channel-count-invariant structural summary of arbitrary low-resolution feature maps and use it to parameterize local image-guided attention whose values remain in the original encoder's feature space.
method.mechanism: A shared bank of 128 spatial filters processes every source-feature channel independently; softmax responses are averaged over channels into canonical key features. A residual RGB encoder produces high-resolution queries, coarse RGB and canonical feature summaries produce keys, and raw coarse encoder features provide values. Relative local-window attention upsamples to an arbitrary requested grid. Training uses ImageNet, random local high-resolution crops as attainable target features, cosine-plus-MSE supervision, clean/noisy guidance self-consistency, and downsampled-output/input-feature consistency.
assumptions: A permutation-invariant average of per-channel spatial responses retains enough local structure to route arbitrary encoder features.
High-resolution feature vectors can be usefully approximated by linear combinations of nearby coarse feature vectors.
RGB edges and local color structure are valid guidance for semantic and geometric feature boundaries rather than a source of texture-copy artifacts.
Crop features are an appropriate target for the corresponding region of a feature map computed from a resized full image despite their different visual context.
The tested encoder and task suite is representative enough to support an inference-time encoder-agnostic claim.

techniques.role: Maps variable-dimensional feature maps into a fixed 128-channel structural summary without learning an encoder-specific projection.
Uses RGB-derived pixel queries to interpolate raw coarse feature values only from a relative neighborhood, reducing distant attention artifacts and cost.
Obtains attainable higher-resolution reference features for sampled regions without a full high-resolution backbone forward pass.
Penalizes disagreement after downsampling the prediction so existing probes can transfer to the upsampled representation.
Reduces dependence on nuisance RGB perturbations by matching predictions from clean and augmented guidance images.

evaluations.setting: DINOv2 ViT-S feature upsampling for COCO-Stuff, ADE20k, and PASCAL-VOC linear semantic probes
evaluations.result: AnyUp reports the best aggregate table entries, including 62.16 COCO mIoU and 42.43 ADE20k mIoU in the extracted table.
evaluations.baseline: Bilinear interpolation, FeatUp, LoftUp, and JAFAR using released weights and a common corrected probe implementation.

evaluations.setting: NYUv2 linear probing for surface normals and monocular absolute/relative depth
evaluations.metric: Normal RMSE and angular accuracy; depth RMSE and delta-1
evaluations.result: AnyUp reports normal RMSE 31.17, absolute-depth RMSE 0.4755/delta-1 0.8216, and relative-depth RMSE 0.3378/delta-1 0.9233, leading the compared methods in the table.
evaluations.baseline: Bilinear interpolation, FeatUp, LoftUp, and JAFAR.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained low-resolution DINOv2 probes applied directly to upsampled features
evaluations.metric: ADE20k segmentation mIoU/accuracy and NYUv2 depth RMSE/delta-1
evaluations.result: AnyUp reports 40.83 mIoU and 74.94 accuracy with depth RMSE 0.498 and delta-1 0.822, whereas LoftUp's segmentation falls to 4.27 mIoU under the same no-retraining test.
evaluations.baseline: Bilinear, guided filtering, FeatUp, LoftUp, and JAFAR with the same frozen probe.

evaluations.setting: Cross-backbone and cross-model-size transfer, including DINOv2-trained upsampling of SigLIP2 and DINOv3 plus five-backbone training with held-out DeiT
evaluations.result: The transferred AnyUp matches or exceeds several encoder-specific baselines; multi-backbone training improves held-out DeiT and average scores but slightly reduces DINOv2 in-domain performance.
evaluations.baseline: Encoder-specific AnyUp, LoftUp, and JAFAR instances and single-DINOv2 AnyUp training.

evaluations.setting: Single-A100 efficiency at several output resolutions and component ablations
evaluations.metric: Parameters, runtime, FLOPs, memory, mIoU, accuracy, and depth RMSE
evaluations.result: The 0.8M-parameter model reports over 50% less runtime and memory than global-attention JAFAR/LoftUp at larger grids, although FeatUp is lighter; every removed component reduces at least one reported task metric and larger filter banks generally help.
evaluations.baseline: FeatUp, LoftUp, JAFAR, no-window, alternative data sampling, removed regularizers, removed feature-key path, and filter-basis sizes 0-256.

limitations: The claimed universality is tested on a finite set dominated by 2D natural-image vision transformers; medical, remote-sensing, video, multimodal, non-grid, and strongly domain-shifted features are not a broad transfer benchmark.
Output features are constrained to the span of nearby coarse input vectors, so information encoded within channels but not expressible by local convex-style mixing cannot be decoded.

Most quantitative comparisons predate three direct 2026 competitors—Weighted Reverse Convolution, RaysUp, and PixelUp—that claim stronger accuracy-efficiency or zero-shot transfer and require common-harness replication.
The paper trains once for 100,000 ImageNet steps on one H100 but does not report seed variance, training-time sensitivity, or a matched total-compute comparison against every competitor.
Several table cells are very close, and no confidence intervals or significance tests establish that small metric differences are repeatable.

High-resolution RGB guidance can insert texture edges into representations; the provided clean benchmarks and qualitative examples do not isolate adversarial texture, low contrast, misregistration, or corrupt guidance.
failure_modes: A target representation uses channel semantics or cross-channel correlations that disappear under permutation-invariant channel averaging, producing weak or ambiguous keys.
A correct correspondence lies outside the fixed local attention window, as with repeated structures, large motion, or nonlocal semantic grouping.
RGB boundaries disagree with semantic boundaries, causing texture copying, halos, or splitting of uniform objects.
The high-resolution feature should contain a vector outside the local coarse-feature span, making faithful recovery impossible regardless of training.
Features with extreme scale, sparsity, normalization, or spatial layout differ from the training mixture and saturate the per-channel softmax basis responses.
A frozen downstream head is sensitive to small distribution changes that the input-consistency loss does not capture.
reusable_insights: When tensor width must remain open at inference time, separate routing from payload: compute permutation-invariant statistics for keys while passing the unknown-width feature itself as the attention value.
Local crop targets can turn otherwise unaffordable dense supervision into a tractable patchwise objective without pretending that resized full-image features are ground truth.
Feature upsampling should be evaluated both with a head retrained on outputs and with an unchanged head; the gap measures representation-space drift rather than only downstream recoverability.
Universal-method claims need leave-one-family-out evaluation, not only leave-one-checkpoint-out evaluation, because same-family encoders share positional and tokenization artifacts.
A newer competitor audit can materially narrow a paper's novelty even when its original first-of-kind statement was reasonable at submission time.
open_questions: Does AnyUp remain competitive with RaysUp, Weighted Reverse Convolution, and PixelUp in one version-pinned training and evaluation harness?
How does performance change under leave-one-architecture-family-out tests spanning convolutional, hierarchical, dense-prediction, video, medical, and remote-sensing encoders?
Can a channel-invariant module retain pairwise or higher-order cross-channel structure without fixing input dimensionality?
What portion of the gain comes from reconstructing latent sub-patch information versus copying high-resolution RGB boundaries into coarse semantics?
Would adaptive or multiscale neighborhoods recover nonlocal correspondence without restoring the quadratic global-attention failure mode?
How well do frozen nonlinear heads, nearest-neighbor retrieval, correspondence, and calibrated uncertainty survive the upsampling transformation?

competitive_landscape.title: FeatUp: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Features at Any Resolution
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational task- and model-agnostic feature densification baseline using learned joint-bilateral or per-image implicit upsampling with multiview consistency.
competitive_landscape.difference: FeatUp preserves semantics and supports many backbones but trains an upsampler for a selected feature source or optimizes per image; AnyUp's shared channel-invariant key path is designed to transfer one learned model to unseen encoder dimensionalities and uses crop supervision rather than multiview reconstruction.

competitive_landscape.title: LoftUp: Learning a Coordinate-Based Feature Upsampler for Vision Foundation Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct arbitrary-resolution attention competitor that creates high-resolution pseudo-targets from class-agnostic masks and self-distillation.
competitive_landscape.difference: LoftUp uses global coordinate-based cross-attention and an encoder-specific feature projection, with mask-blended targets that can change feature geometry. AnyUp uses local attention, raw features as values, and source/crop consistency to transfer across encoder widths and preserve a frozen probe's feature space.

competitive_landscape.title: JAFAR: Jack up Any Feature at Any Resolution
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest architectural predecessor: high-resolution image queries attend to low-resolution semantic keys and raw feature values at arbitrary output scales.
competitive_landscape.difference: JAFAR learns fixed-dimensional encoder-specific feature processing and global attention from low-ratio supervision. AnyUp replaces that projection with a shared per-channel filter basis, localizes attention, and uses original-resolution local crops for targets; despite JAFAR's title, its released learned instance is not one-model cross-encoder inference.

competitive_landscape.title: Weighted Reverse Convolution for Feature Upsampling
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-submission direct competitor that treats VFM densification as a spatially weighted inverse problem rather than learned feature interpolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: WRC solves a weighted Tikhonov-regularized reverse-convolution problem with a differentiable closed-form FFT operator and reports segmentation, depth, video segmentation, discovery, and correspondence. AnyUp learns RGB-guided local attention and demonstrates explicit cross-encoder width transfer; the paper contains no WRC comparison because WRC appeared later.

competitive_landscape.title: RaysUp: Ultra-light Universal Feature Upsampling via Geometry-Aware Ray Representation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-submission universal, task-agnostic, VFM-agnostic arbitrary-resolution upsampler and therefore a direct challenge to AnyUp's current accuracy-efficiency position.
competitive_landscape.difference: RaysUp injects 6D Plucker-ray positional geometry, spatially decoupled guidance, arbitrary-resolution cross-attention, and neighborhood attention; its abstract claims 16% of AnyUp's parameters and roughly sevenfold faster inference. AnyUp instead obtains invariance by pooling shared filter responses across channels and needs a reproducible common-hardware comparison to retain an efficiency claim.

competitive_landscape.title: PixelUp: Zero-Shot Semantic Feature Upsampling for Fine-Grained Vision Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Newest located zero-shot VFM-agnostic competitor, motivated by texture artifacts and missing semantic guidance in image-guided upsamplers.
competitive_landscape.difference: PixelUp uses a coarse-to-fine chain of windowed cross-attention guided by multiscale semantic features and reports improvements over VFM-specific and VFM-agnostic methods. AnyUp uses a single local attention layer and shallow RGB guidance; PixelUp's later results narrow AnyUp's state-of-the-art claim but its broader cost, feature-space preservation, and channel-dimensional invariance require direct verification.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors present AnyUp as the first trainable, task-agnostic feature upsampler that can be trained once and then applied at inference time to any encoder dimensionality and any input/output resolution, enabled by a feature-agnostic layer plus local attention and crop-based training.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Relative to FeatUp, LoftUp, and JAFAR available around submission, the distinctive combination is credible: keys are built with a variable-width channel-invariant filter bank, values remain in the source space, and experiments include truly held-out encoder types. The main empirical suite reports strong dense-task and frozen-probe performance. However, the attention and crop-supervision components are adaptations of existing methods, transfer coverage is finite, and 2026 WRC, RaysUp, and PixelUp now directly compete with or claim to surpass the universal feature-upsampling position.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The durable novelty is the routing/payload factorization that permits one learned attention module to accept unseen channel dimensions, not a timeless claim to universal state of the art. Current novelty should be stated as an early explicit one-model cross-encoder solution with strong feature-space preservation. Accuracy and efficiency superiority are now unverified against later direct competitors, and 'any encoder' remains a hypothesis outside the tested 2D vision family.

Numeric entries were taken only where the PDF extraction kept table-row alignment intelligible; several dense tables are visually interleaved in the text cache, so the synthesis avoids reconstructing uncertain cells. The competitor audit used mechanism, benchmark/baseline, and novelty-language searches across arXiv, OpenReview, and official CVF proceedings on 2026-08-23. It adds three later direct competitors absent from the paper. This is a primary full-text pass, not an independent secondary verification.
